title: spec(data): a date or datetime field declares its deadline semantic — `dueLike` with `settledWhen` (per-record CEL), so overdue wording and colour derive from one declaration and the name-pattern guess retires (objectui#11815 ruled D)
body:
Filing gate: **③ a maintainer-directed task**, the protocol half of objectui#11815's ruling D. Filed by the director seat (seat post #12708, summon #35, `session_01VYToj6PQehTEKNrjGM9akg`). The maintainer's words on objectui#11815: 「每个状态不是可以自己配置颜色吗?done 配置为红色不是元数据的 bug 吗?为什么平台要兜一圈」, then 「同意」 to the seat's option D (declared-only overdue: no name guessing, the deadline declares when it is settled). ⛔ Not a claim.

Reader: the `domain:spec` seat. `Clause-②: yes` — the published accept set of the date and datetime field definitions widens by two keys; the spec-lane review at tier applies. `priority:p3` (cosmetic today; nothing is stored wrong). objectui#11815 is `Blocked-by:` this card and lands after the spec publishes.

## Why the protocol, and not objectui alone

- objectui's date cells decide "overdue" from two guesses and never read the record (`packages/fields/src/index.tsx`, `resolveDueLike` and `isOverdueInstant`): a field is due-like when its runtime metadata carries `dueLike: true` **or** its name matches `/(^|_)(due|deadline|expires?|expiry|expiration|expected_close|target_close|sla|return_by|renewal|next_action)(_|$)/`; a due-like date before today paints `text-red-600` and the wording "Overdue Nd". A finished record stays red for ever.
- `dueLike` is an objectui-owned key (objectui#9738, ruled A on 2026-09-18: "objectui-owned until the protocol claims it"), declared on objectui's `DateFieldMetadata` (`packages/types/src/field-types.ts`) and enriched from the detail-view field config. The protocol's view schemas are strict and their passthrough window is shut (`packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`), so an application validated by `@objectstack/spec` — the example apps, hotcrm — cannot author `dueLike` at all. Today the only way a date goes red is the name guess.
- A deadline is a semantic of the field, not a style of one view: "this date is a deadline, settled when the record's status is done" belongs on the field definition, and wording, colour, and later filters, metrics and an agent's answer to "what is overdue" all derive from it. That is the positioning (the ontology is the software), and it is monday.com's Deadline Mode shape (a date column linked to a status column whose Done labels settle it). A style rule cannot carry the wording and would be re-authored per view (the field-level `conditionalFormatting` card filed beside this one is for presentational rules without a semantic).

## What this card adds, and only this

On the `date` and `datetime` field definitions (`packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts`):

- `dueLike: boolean` (optional, default absent) — this field is a deadline; a renderer may show relative overdue wording and an overdue affordance for it. ⛔ No name-pattern inference anywhere: absent means not a deadline.
- `settledWhen` (optional) — a per-record CEL predicate in the `visibleWhen` / `readonlyWhen` / `requiredWhen` family, evaluated against the record; when it holds the deadline is settled and no overdue wording or affordance applies (for example `record.status == 'done'`, or `record.done == true`). Authoring-gate rules as for its siblings: it parses, or the metadata is refused with a prescription; `settledWhen` without `dueLike` is refused (ADR-0049: a declared key is enforced).
- The ADR-0087 conversion entry, generated baselines and forms, the docs page that teaches `visibleWhen`, a pin test for the gate and for the two scope names.
- Example apps declare it where the semantic is real: showcase `task` (`due_date`, settled on `status == 'done'`), app-todo `task` (settled on `status == 'completed'`), crm `activity` (settled on `status == 'completed'`), so the example grids keep their overdue affordance after objectui retires the guess.

Changeset: `@objectstack/spec` minor.

## ⛔ Not this card

- No terminal marker on select options (the seat's option A on objectui#11815, not taken): "finished" stays local to the deadline that cares, expressed as a predicate; a protocol-level terminal concept can be declared later and `settledWhen` can then read it.
- No change in objectui: objectui#11815 (blocked by this card) retires the name regex, reads `dueLike` and the host-evaluated `settledWhen` through one optional cell prop, and decides whether its mirror's view-level `dueLike` is retired or kept as an override.

Dedupe: the 128 open objectstack issues listed through the repository endpoint and scanned (title and body) for dueLike / settledWhen / overdue / terminal option / 逾期: 0. Prior rulings read: objectui#9738 (`dueLike` objectui-owned until the protocol claims it — this card is the protocol claiming it), objectui#11676 ruling A (no guessing a record's state), objectui#11815 ruling D → 3 hits; ADR-0049, ADR-0087.
